editorial:
Imagine stepping back into old Paris where the huge bells of Notre Dame ring out over a city full of secrets. You will meet Quasimodo, a kind man with a deformed face who just wants to be loved, and Esmeralda, a beautiful dancer who sees the heart inside the monster. The vibe is a mix of a sad love story and a creepy thriller. You will quickly realize that the real monster is actually Frollo, the judge who uses his power to hurt people while pretending to be a holy man. It is a heavy story, but it keeps you hooked because you just want the good guys to win.

What really stands out is the acting, especially how they make you feel for Quasimodo. The movie moves at a decent pace, though some parts feel a bit slow by today's standards. If you like old Hollywood classics with big emotions, you will love this. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you really love the old-school look, you should add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection to see the details of the cathedral. It is definitely a great pick for a rainy weekend night.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Frollo tries to force Esmeralda to love him or die. Quasimodo saves her by bringing her into the cathedral, but Frollo's soldiers attack anyway. In the end, Frollo falls to his death from the top of the cathedral. Quasimodo is left heartbroken as he finds Esmeralda dead, and he stays by her side in a sad, final moment of love.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old classics and tragic love stories.
